title: Zero Array Transformation II
summary: Given an integer array nums and a series of queries, each query specifies a range and a value.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a series of queries, each query specifies a range and a value. Each query allows decrementing the values in the specified range by at most the given value. Determine the minimum number of queries needed to make nums a Zero Array, or return -1 if it's impossible.
constraints: nums and queries each contain up to 100,000 entries; query values are positive.
Within each prefix query, every covered index independently receives any decrement from zero through val.
Return the shortest query prefix whose capacities cover nums, zero if already zero, or -1 if all queries fail.
reference_solution:
def minimum_zero_array_queries(nums,queries):
    def possible(count):
        difference=[0]*(len(nums)+1)
        for left,right,value in queries[:count]:difference[left]+=value;difference[right+1]-=value
        capacity=0
        for index,need in enumerate(nums):
            capacity+=difference[index]
            if need>capacity:return False
        return True
    low=0;high=len(queries)+1
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        if possible(middle):high=middle
        else:low=middle+1
    return -1 if low>len(queries) else low

hints: Feasibility is monotone: adding another query never removes decrement capacity.
Binary-search the prefix length and test it with a weighted difference array.
For a candidate prefix, sum range values at each index and require capacity >= nums[i].
Independent per-index decrement choices make the capacity test exact, and monotonicity makes lower-bound search valid.
